subject: Renewal paperwork: proposed term change + exhibit alignment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@silverline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal paperwork: proposed term change + exhibit alignment

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Per our conversation, attached is a clean summary of the proposed changes for Silverline's renewal: a shift from a 12‑month to a 24‑month term, an Exhibit F update for data retention, and an order form amendment to reflect the 25% capacity uplift we discussed.

Highlights:
- Term: Redwood proposes a 24‑month renewal (effective 10/01/2026) in exchange for a multi‑year commitment credit.
- Capacity: Order form shows +25% committed capacity (see line items 2–4).
- Exhibit F: Clarify retention window (90 days KV cache, 365 days logs) and add language for audit log export (SLA change).
- Indemnity / IP: We marked a neutral position but flagged the paragraph where Silverline requested an indemnity cap change.

Please review the attached redlines (Silverline_Renewal_Redlines_v3.docx) and let me know the high‑level items your procurement/legal will want to escalate. I'm proposing the following mutual action plan:
1) You return any counter‑redlines by Sep 2
2) We loop in Laura (legal) and Ben (pricing) for a single consolidated reply
3) If both sides agree on the material changes, we prepare a single orderform amendment + MSA mark‑up for signature via DocuSign.

If helpful I can offer a 10% one‑time credit applied to Q4 invoices if Silverline signs the 24‑month commitment by Sep 16.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Silverline_Renewal_Redlines_v3.docx, OrderForm_Amendment_20260831.pdf

From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@silverline.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harwood <tom.harwood@silverline.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@silverline.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork: proposed term change + exhibit alignment

Rachel —

Thanks for the summary and the fast turnaround. A few quick items from procurement/legal's side after an initial read:
- Term: 24 months is plausible but procurement needs clarity on early termination and proration language. Can Redwood add an early termination clause example with proration mechanics?
- Indemnity cap: our legal team is pushing to keep it at 1x annual fees; they redlined the clause and proposed narrowing the scope for third‑party claims.
- Data retention: we need confirmation that log exports can be disabled on request, and a statement about customer‑owned encryption keys for the Private deployment option.

I attached our counter‑redlines as well (we marked the indemnity and early termination sections). We also need SOC 2 evidence and the latest DPA. Procurement will compile questions and aim to send the consolidated redline by Sep 2 EOD.

Appreciate the proposed credit — that will help the business case.

Emily
Senior Procurement Manager, Silverline Systems
Attachment: Silverline_Counter_Redlines_v1.docx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal paperwork: proposed term change + exhibit alignment

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Silverline's initial reply and counter‑redlines. Key asks from procurement/legal: early termination proration mechanics, indemnity cap at 1x ARR, and confirmation on DPA / customer KMS for Private option.

Ask list:
- Ben: can you confirm impact of a 24‑month commitment + 10% credit on our revenue recognition / pricing? I'd like a short writeup (1 paragraph) we can include in the consolidated response.
- Laura: can you review Silverline's indemnity and early termination redlines and propose alternative language that protects Redwood but keeps the business case intact?
- Marissa: I'll own the reply and will incorporate Ben/Laura's inputs; please let me know if you want me to offer a phased signature approach (MSA now, orderform amendment later).

Tentative timeline: consolidate internal comments by EOD Sep 1, send to Emily Sep 2 so they can review before their legal meeting on Sep 6.

Thanks —
Rachel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal paperwork: proposed term change + exhibit alignment

All — thanks for the quick turnaround. I reviewed Emily's counter‑redlines and drafted proposed language in the attached response (see: Redwood_Response_Redlines_v1.docx). Summary of our position and next steps:

1) Early termination/proration: Acceptable to provide explicit proration example — nominate pro‑rata refund for unused months with a 60‑day notice window. Laura, I drafted a tight clause that limits liability and avoids lookback calculations.
2) Indemnity cap: We should hold firm at a negotiated cap (1.5x ARR) rather than 1x; that's a reasonable middle ground. Laura's draft contains a carve that narrows third‑party claim scope.
3) Data retention & KMS: Confirm we support customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted, we offer customer‑managed encryption keys via partner HSM (we can provide a technical note and SOC 2 link). Ben — please attach the hosting support note.
4) Commercial credit: I'm ok with the 10% one‑time Q4 credit, but recommend tying approval to a signature by Sep 16 and a minimum committed spend threshold.

Action items:
- Laura: finalize indemnity + termination language by EOD Sep 2
- Ben: draft short pricing impact paragraph and hosting/KMS note
- Rachel: consolidate and send to Emily Sep 2 morning (PST) with attachments and DocuSign prepped if they accept the language.

I'll review the final package before send.

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Response_Redlines_v1.docx
